claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ (the Terraform state backend guide) exists.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN may be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate domain or second DNS record is not required.

The Terraform state backend guide uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the Terraform-compatible API domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

Terraform's `terraform login` and OpenTofu's `tofu login` commands, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` environment variable name (which encodes the domain), are used to authenticate against the Terraform-compatible API domain.
